themes.title: Nvidia enters post-Huang era with succession in play
themes.summary: Days after Jensen Huang's exit, Nvidia's leadership vacuum is filling fast: Arm boss Rene Haas has been sounded out for the CEO seat and interim chief Colette Kress faces scrutiny heading into Tuesday's earnings. The open question of whether Huang's ~$135bn stake gets sold, plus a $500bn funding hole in the wider AI capex cycle, frames the stakes for everyone riding Nvidia's fortunes.
themes.angle: Founder dependency meets the $500bn AI capex cycle - boards should stress-test concentration.

themes.title: Anthropic's $1.5tn IPO test
themes.summary: Anthropic has filed its S-1, kicked off its roadshow and named an expected $1.5tn listing - a live referendum on whether public markets still price frontier AI at its peak. Its CEO says he is not fussed by the recent tech turbulence; a jailed FTX founder's early stake would have paid out nearly $40bn at that valuation.
themes.angle: The float's reception becomes the real test of AI capex confidence this quarter.

themes.title: GCC AI capex hits scale: SAR 2.5bn, $9bn, and IPO gaps
themes.summary: Gulf capital is moving in volume: Saudi-linked HUMAIN and Infra signed SAR 2.5bn of AI data-centre financing, Dubai's Damac committed $9bn to US data centres, and Abu Dhabi-backed Nscale warns of a funding gap ahead of its own IPO. EDGE's $50m bet on quantum navigation and Cerebras' amended MBZUAI compute agreement round out a region spending before it builds.
themes.angle: The GCC is becoming a bankroller of global AI infrastructure, not just a buyer of it.

themes.title: Fed flags AI as top financial-stability risk
themes.summary: The Fed's semi-annual stability report and a separate survey both surfaced AI and AI-driven asset valuations as the top worries for the financial system, with AI rocketing to the front of the risk ranking. Regulators are now treating AI concentration and its valuation froth as macro-prudential concerns.
themes.angle: A formal central-bank flag that AI concentration is systemic - boards take note.

themes.title: UAE and Saudi press the AI-adoption message
themes.summary: Gulf AI ambition stayed in the spotlight: Altman called the UAE the world's most forward-looking country on AI adoption, Dubai unveiled the Nad Zabeel innovation campus targeting 30,000 researchers a year, and Etisalat launched an AI marketing hub for SMBs. Saudi media pushed a national talent-and-competitiveness framing for women in AI.
themes.angle: The Gulf is pricing human capital and adoption posture as AI policy - a positioning signal.

themes.title: US AI policy: liability relief to buy disclosure
themes.summary: The White House AI task force, at its second meeting, discussed cyber threats to critical infrastructure and is urging agencies to ease cyber-liability rules so companies report AI incidents more freely. The posture pairs deregulation with a disclosure bargain on AI incidents.
themes.angle: An early shape for how the US will govern frontier AI security and disclosure.

themes.title: Single-vendor resilience retested after Microsoft outage
themes.summary: A Microsoft-wide outage that hit banks, governments and pharmacies into a 'broad recovery' has reopened the concentration-of-dependence question, with the FBI separately probing whether a software update, not an attack, caused a mass FAA outage. For GCC CIOs running on US hyperscalers, it is a resilience wake-up call.
themes.angle: Hosting-dependency risk becomes a live board question again.

themes.title: Frontier labs push agents to transact and verify
themes.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet so agents can complete purchases with user approval, DeepMind shipped AlphaProof Code for verifying complex software at depth, and Anthropic rounded out its Opus/Haiku 5.5 line with a Claude-run marketplace experiment. The through-line is agents moving from chat to spending and proving.
themes.angle: The agentic layer is getting money rails and proof machinery - watch both.
